Legislators are experts at designing statutes to take advantage

of the blind spots of “discrete, atomized voters.” Not only is the 1970 Clean Air Act a case in point, but subsequent amendments to it reflected new twists to maximize credit and minimize blame.41 Unlike the pre-1970 air pollution statute, the current version is full of detailed statutory commands such as the 940 instances of “shall” in the Clean Air Act that protect Congress from accusations that it handed a blank check to the agency.
